fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Alchenomics and the reverse alchemy of currency", "body": "Chance Garton brings in Tracy Twyman's book Money Grows on the Tree of Knowledge to argue that modern currency is an alchemical working, a transformation of debt into imagined value through the collective mind. Parallel Mike agrees but flips the direction, calling it reverse alchemy. In his telling, money began as a rare metal that stored finite human time and effort, and the system has turned that gold back into lead, then into digits on a screen that carry value only because somebody says they do. Chance notes that the architects of the system still run one of the oldest economic journals."}, {"title": "A gangster's son learning what money does to people", "body": "Parallel Mike tells how he learned his father was one of the biggest figures in British crime, hearing his own name on the radio at about ten after the largest cannabis resin smuggle into the UK. He describes rolls of fifty pound notes and cash in the cookie jar, then the sudden famine of life with a single mother on minimum wage. That swing from feast to famine turned him off money entirely. He studied theology, Buddhism and existential philosophy, became a counsellor and an ultra runner, and only later came back to economics."}, {"title": "Energy embodiments and a parasitic second tier", "body": "Mike's central economic idea is the energy embodiment. Anything pulled from the earth, whether gold, a clay brick, food or fuel, stores the finite time and effort spent extracting it, and gold sits at the top because it never tarnishes and is extremely hard to get. He argues civilisation grew a second tier of finance, business, media and marketing that consumes energy embodiments without any connection to Mother Nature, and that this arrangement is parasitic. In his view, farmers and lumberjacks are impoverished and subsidised while the people furthest from the soil are rewarded most."}, {"title": "Lead, gold and the correspondences behind metals", "body": "Chance shares a tarot pull from one of his tuning sessions, the Devil card, a Capricorn card ruled by Saturn, which corresponds to lead, and says the correspondence proved strikingly apt, which to him shows these planetary and metal correspondences are real. From there he argues that gold stores solar and life giving energy, so replacing it with emptiness leaves empty professions behind. Mike extends the idea to the ages of gold, silver, bronze, iron and now lead, and says that when currency is debased, morality is debased alongside it."}, {"title": "Existential debt, pensions and building parallel systems", "body": "Mike argues the system has convinced people of existential debt, a theological trick where Christ's atonement is replaced by money as the savior and every child is born owing what can never be repaid. He rejects it, insisting you are born free, and recommends gold because it carries no counterparty risk and sits outside the system, unlike land that can be taxed or confiscated. Chance closes with Webster's 1828 definitions of pension, arguing that accepting one means accepting you are disabled, and prefers land, family and self sufficiency as real security."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mike from the Parallel Systems Broadcast joins InnerVerse to discuss the psychology of wealth. Mike's journey from paranoid to parallel is explored, as is alchenomics, money vs. wealth, correspondences to precious metals, the messiah-op, and the religion of existential debt (original sin).
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the 2nd hour, we get into the healthy mindset for generating, Mike's escape from the city to homestead life in Poland, the morality of gold, the slavery of guilt, the crypto casino, how to use precious metals, underground architecture and esoteric Poland. All that and more!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Rewiring the mind before the money", "body": "Mike traces his method back to running, where he cut his career to two days a week, ran a hundred miles a week, and still found that effort alone would never let him beat athletes who had been competing for decades. His coach told him the mileage mattered less than the non running work, so he built visualizations and affirmations until the subconscious accepted the outcome in advance. When injury ended that career he ran the same exercise again, spending seven or eight years studying money, its history, investing and the different asset classes the way he had once studied training."}, {"title": "Holistic wealth instead of digits", "body": "Pressed on what wealth actually means, Mike refuses the screen full of digits and defines it as capacity: time with family, physical health, relationships, and an income that does not oblige him to serve a system he finds immoral. He then points out how little money that takes. He and his wife spent their small savings on a tiny boat rather than rent or a mortgage, cut their outgoings to almost nothing, and later moved onto land with solar panels and a well they dug. Friends who scraped together a lump sum for a plot are, he says, flying."}, {"title": "Self worth as the gate on abundance", "body": "Chance maps the block to the sacral centre, the orange energy whose imbalance shows as frustration on one side and guilt and shame on the other. Because sin is defined as debt, a business model built on fleecing the other party leaves a residue of shame that closes the channel abundance would come through. His remedy is a switch to win win dealing, unresolved frustration worked through rather than carried, and a deliberate gratitude practice at meals, traced back through farmers and drivers, until the body itself produces the pleasurable feeling of satisfaction at the sight of food."}, {"title": "A parcel returned at real cost", "body": "Mike tells of jewellery bought for his wife that a driver left over the fence while the family was away. The company posted a replacement, the original then turned up, and holding two of them, worth roughly three months of salary, he called and sent one back, not out of any feeling for the courier company but because the driver would otherwise have been charged for it or lost his job. He offers it as the shape a core set of principles takes around money, alongside his own answer to why the very rich go unpunished: awful health, awful relationships."}, {"title": "Money that is not imbued with nature", "body": "The Bitcoin stretch turns on a symbol Chance spots first, that a gold coin used to be tested by biting it, so the newest currency borrows the name of the oldest test. Mike then applies his own criterion, that money must be imbued with nature, and anything abstracted from nature's economy fails it whatever its code. He treats Bitcoin as a useful technology that will be superseded like the railroad and early automotive companies, worries it softened the public for central bank digital currency, and calls speculation gambling while Chance reads the 1828 dictionary entry on lotteries."}]
